newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech CEZ shares regain 1,000 crown level.
newsitem.headline: Czech CEZ shares regain 1,000 crown level.

text.p: Shares in Czech power utility CEZ a.s. on Tuesday crossed the 1,000 crown mark for the first time since last October driven mainly by domestic buying, dealers said.

At 1152 GMT (1252 local time) CEZ was up 23 crowns, 2.3 percent, to 1,011 and dealers on the bourse said there was likely to be sufficient support to keep the share above 1,000 crowns for the rest of the day.
"I have been quoting at 1,005/1,115 in the last half hour. The price is pretty stable," said Pavel Slanbor of Zivnostenska Banka.
CEZ is the Czech Republic's largest company by revenue and is generally regarded is a cheap entry point for investors interested in Czech blue chip issues.

However, the company's share price suffered more than many other major issues in the general downturn on the Prague bourse, which began in late September, because of fears over tight government control over electricity prices.
Slanbor said Tuesday's demand for CEZ was mainly domestic in origin although some foreign buying had been seen.
